newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen flat-off $0.50-trade.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by slipping pork prices, livestock dealers said.
Pork cut-out values late Monday were quoted $0.34 per cwt lower on all grade carcasses, USDA said.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa and southern Minnesota were seen ranging from $49.50 to $50.50, sources there said. Illinois top prices at plants could range $49.50 to $50.50.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs at the plant could range $49.50 to $50.00, dealers said.
Hog prices also were pressured by adequate hog supplies amid light packer demand, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog movement was estimated at 100,000 head, compared with 98,000 a week ago, USDA said.
One buyer for a major packer said that company had booked enough hogs for Tuesday's slaughter and would be bidding $0.50 lower for Wednesday's production.
